sentences.text: This animal reached a length of 5 to 6 meters and a weight between 454 and 907 kilograms, though some estimates suggest it was around 600 kg.
It is distinguished by long slender limbs, a long and slender humerus, a robust and curved first digit, and a femur and tibia of subequal length.
A 2001 study found no signs of stress fractures in 23 foot bones examined from Alectrosaurus.
The genus Alectrosaurus was formally described by Charles Gilmore in 1933, and the genus and species were named by American paleontologist Charles W. Gilmore in 1933.
The name Alectrosaurus translates to 'alone lizard' or 'mateless lizard', derived from Greek words meaning alone and lizard, because no two skeletons were ever found together.
The species name olseni honors George Olsen, the discoverer of the first specimens.
The type specimen of Alectrosaurus was a hind limb discovered in the Iren Dabasu Formation in Inner Mongolia, China.
A second specimen, catalogued as AMNH 6368, was discovered by George Olsen approximately 30 meters away from the holotype on May 4.
Alectrosaurus was likely a fast-running pursuit predator, a trait indicated by its elongated hindlimbs that was lost in later, more robust tyrannosaurids.
The animal has a high cursorial-limb-proportion score of 16.5, which is higher than most carnosaurs.
Alectrosaurus and Gigantoraptor were the top predators of their paleoenvironment and preyed on ornithischians like Bactrosaurus and Gilmoreosaurus.
Gilmore classified Alectrosaurus as a 'Deinodont,' a term now considered equivalent to tyrannosaurid, based on similarities in manual unguals and hindlimbs.
Alectrosaurus was originally characterized as a theropod with long arms, but this was due to a mistaken association with forelimb elements from a Therizinosauroidea.
Alectrosaurus lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 96 million years ago, in the Iren Dabasu Formation.
The age of the Iren Dabasu Formation is unclear, but it is commonly cited as Campanian, Late Cretaceous, approximately 83 to 74 million years ago.
The time range for Alectrosaurus is estimated from the Cenomanian to Campanian stages, between 100.5 and 72.2 million years ago.
Additional fossils, including hind limb material, a skull, and shoulder elements, referred to Alectrosaurus were found in the Bayan Shireh Formation of Mongolia, which also has an uncertain age.
Due to its fragmentary nature, there is little confidence in Alectrosaurus's relationships with other tyrannosauroids, and many recent analyses have omitted it.
Some paleontologists have considered Alectrosaurus olseni to be a species of Albertosaurus.
In 2022, Thomas Carr suggested that certain Mongolian specimens previously linked to Alectrosaurus may not belong to the genus due to unique tyrannosaurid traits.
A cladistic analysis showed that collections of specimens relate more to each other than to any other taxon, suggesting they are at least closely linked, if not the same species.
